questions.question_text: In adults, the spinal cord ends at: (2019 - 2020).
questions.check_explanation: In adults the conus medullaris typically ends at the level of the lower border of the L1 vertebral body (around L1‑L2 disc).

check_why_others_wrong.b: L3 is too low for the conus medullaris.
check_why_others_wrong.c: S1 is far below the normal termination level.
check_why_others_wrong.d: Duplicate of L3, also too low.

questions.question_text: A patient came to emergency room presenting with headache; fever, nausea and stiffness of the neck. He was diagnosed as meningitis. What is the name of the procedure by which a special needle is inserted into the subarachnoid space to get sample of CSF to confirm the diagnosis? (2018 – 2017 - 2016).
questions.check_explanation: Lumbar puncture is the procedure of inserting a needle into the lumbar subarachnoid space to obtain CSF.

check_why_others_wrong.a: Conus medullaris is an anatomical structure, not a procedure.
check_why_others_wrong.b: Lumbar cistern is the CSF-filled space, not the name of the technique.
check_why_others_wrong.d: Cauda equina refers to nerve roots, not the sampling method.

questions.question_text: Cauda equina is: (2018).

options.label: a
options.text: The lower segments of the spinal cord.

options.label: b
options.text: The roots of lower lumbar, sacral and coccygeal nerves.

options.label: c
options.text: The spinal nerves of the conus medullaris.

options.label: d
options.text: The spinal nerves of the lower lumbar and sacral segments.

questions.check_explanation: Cauda equina is the bundle of descending lumbar, sacral and coccygeal nerve roots below the conus medullaris.

check_why_others_wrong.a: Refers to spinal cord segments, not the nerve root bundle.
check_why_others_wrong.c: Describes nerves of the conus medullaris, not the descending roots.
check_why_others_wrong.d: Omits coccygeal roots and mentions spinal nerves instead of roots.

questions.question_text: The spinal cord has ...... select the best statement (DEP BOOK).

options.label: a
options.text: An outer covering of gray matter and an inner core of white matter.

options.label: b
options.text: Anterior and posterior roots of a single spinal nerve attached to a single segment.

options.label: c
options.text: Cells in the posterior gray horn give rise to efferent fibers that supply skeletal muscle.

options.label: d
options.text: A central canal that is situated in the white commissure.

questions.check_explanation: Each spinal nerve is formed by ventral (anterior) and dorsal (posterior) roots that attach to the same spinal segment.

check_why_others_wrong.a: Gray matter is central, white matter surrounds it
check_why_others_wrong.c: Posterior horn contains sensory neurons, not motor efferents
check_why_others_wrong.d: Central canal lies within gray matter, not the white commissure

questions.question_text: If we need to insert a needle into the subarachnoid space to sample CSF, where is a relatively safe point for needle insertion? (DEP BOOK).
questions.check_explanation: Lumbar puncture is safely performed below the conus medullaris, typically at the L3‑L4 interspace, avoiding risk to the spinal cord.

check_why_others_wrong.a: Cervical region is unsafe for CSF sampling; cord is present.
check_why_others_wrong.c: L1‑L2 is at the level of the conus medullaris, risking cord injury.
check_why_others_wrong.d: T12‑L1 is above the conus medullaris, also unsafe.

questions.question_text: In newborns, conus medullaris lies opposite the: (2021 – IPKA - 2023).
questions.check_explanation: In newborns the spinal cord ends at the L2‑L3 level, corresponding roughly to the third lumbar vertebra.

check_why_others_wrong.a: T10 is far above the typical newborn conus level.
check_why_others_wrong.b: L1 is lower than the newborn conus, which is around L2‑L3.
check_why_others_wrong.d: L5 is far below the conus medullaris in any age.

questions.question_text: One of the following arteries is not supplying spinal cord: (2021).
questions.check_explanation: The medial spinal artery is not a recognized vessel that supplies the spinal cord, whereas the radicular branches of the vertebral artery, posterior spinal artery, and anterior spinal artery all contribute to cord perfusion.

check_why_others_wrong.a: Radicular branches of the vertebral artery form part of the segmental supply to the cord.
check_why_others_wrong.b: Posterior spinal arteries supply the dorsal columns of the cord.
check_why_others_wrong.d: Anterior spinal artery supplies the anterior two‑thirds of the cord.

questions.question_text: The true statement about the spinal cord is: (2020  - 2019).

options.label: a
options.text: The spinal dura end at the level of S4.

options.label: c
options.text: The filum terminal is a fold of pia below the termination of spinal cord attached to the. coccyx.

options.label: d
options.text: The largest radicular artery is that of S2.

questions.check_explanation: The filum terminale is a slender extension of pia mater that continues below the conus medullaris and attaches to the coccyx.

check_why_others_wrong.a: The dural sac ends at S2, not S4.
check_why_others_wrong.b: The spinal cord has two enlargements (cervical and lumbar).
check_why_others_wrong.d: The largest radicular artery is the artery of Adamkiewicz, usually arising from T9‑L2, not S2.

questions.question_text: Cauda equine, choose one true statement: (2020).

options.label: a
options.text: Formed of all thoracic and lumber nerves.

options.label: b
options.text: Occupy lower part of spinal canal.

options.label: c
options.text: Surrounded by the three layers of the meninges.

options.label: d
options.text: Pass through the sacrum to end at S2.

questions.check_explanation: Both statements b (occupy lower part of spinal canal) and c (surrounded by the three meningeal layers) are correct, so the question does not have a unique true option.

check_why_others_wrong.a: Cauda equina consists of lumbar, sacral and coccygeal roots, not thoracic
check_why_others_wrong.d: Nerve roots exit at several sacral levels, not all ending at S2

questions.question_text: The lower end of spinal cord is called: (2019).
questions.check_explanation: The tapered terminal portion of the spinal cord is the conus medullaris.

check_why_others_wrong.a: Cauda equina is the nerve root bundle below the conus.
check_why_others_wrong.b: Denticulate ligament is a pia mater extension, not the cord end.
check_why_others_wrong.d: Ganglion impar is a solitary sympathetic ganglion at the coccyx.

questions.question_text: Filum terminal is attached to: (IPKA).
questions.check_explanation: The filum terminale extends from the conus medullaris to attach to the posterior surface of the first coccygeal vertebra.

check_why_others_wrong.a: S3 is a sacral vertebra, not the attachment site.
check_why_others_wrong.b: S4 is also a sacral vertebra, not the attachment site.
check_why_others_wrong.c: The foramen magnum is the cranial opening, unrelated to the filum terminale.

questions.question_text: Lumbar puncture can be done safely: (IPKA).
questions.check_explanation: Lumbar puncture is performed below the conus medullaris, typically at the L3‑L4 interspace, to avoid spinal cord injury.

check_why_others_wrong.a: Too high; spinal cord may be present
check_why_others_wrong.c: Sacral region not used for lumbar puncture
check_why_others_wrong.d: Thoracic level is above spinal cord termination

questions.question_text: Anterior spinal artery supplies: (IPKA).
questions.check_explanation: The anterior spinal artery supplies the anterior two-thirds of the spinal cord, providing blood to the ventral horns and corticospinal tracts.

check_why_others_wrong.a: Posterior 2/3 is supplied by posterior spinal arteries, not anterior.
check_why_others_wrong.b: Lateral 2/3 is not a standard vascular territory; the anterior artery supplies ventral and central regions.
check_why_others_wrong.c: Posterior 1/3 is supplied by posterior spinal arteries.

questions.question_text: Regarding the spinal cord, select the true statement: (2023).

options.label: a
options.text: The lumbosacral enlargement called conus medullaris.

options.label: b
options.text: Denticulate ligament are lateral extension of arachnoid.

options.label: c
options.text: The adult spinal cord terminates at intervertebral disc between L2 and L3.

options.label: d
options.text: The filum terminale attach the lower end of spinal cord with the back of coccyx.

questions.check_explanation: The filum terminale (pia mater) extends from the conus medullaris to the coccyx, anchoring the spinal cord.

check_why_others_wrong.a: Conus medullaris is the tapered tip, not the lumbosacral enlargement.
check_why_others_wrong.b: Denticulate ligaments are extensions of pia mater, not arachnoid.
check_why_others_wrong.c: In adults the cord ends around L1‑L2, not L2‑L3.

questions.question_text: The arterial supply of the lumber enlargement of the spinal cord: (2024).
questions.check_explanation: The great radicular artery (arteria radicularis magna) is the principal feeder to the lumbar enlargement of the spinal cord.

check_why_others_wrong.b: Anterior spinal artery is reinforced by the great radicular artery but is not the main source.
check_why_others_wrong.c: Posterior spinal arteries supply dorsal columns, not the main supply to the enlargement.
check_why_others_wrong.d: Basilar artery supplies the brain, not the spinal cord.

questions.question_text: Concerning spinal nerve C-8, which of the following is true? (DEP BOOK).

options.label: a
options.text: C-8 enters/exits between vertebrae C6 and C7.

options.label: b
options.text: C-8 enters/exits between vertebrae C7 and C8.

options.label: c
options.text: C-8 enters/exits between vertebrae C7 and C8.

options.label: d
options.text: C-8 enters/exits between vertebrae C7 and T1.

questions.check_explanation: The C8 spinal nerve exits below the C7 vertebra, i.e., between the C7 and T1 vertebrae.

check_why_others_wrong.a: C6-C7 level corresponds to C6 nerve, not C8.
check_why_others_wrong.b: There is no vertebra C8; C8 does not exit here.
check_why_others_wrong.c: Duplicate of b and equally incorrect.

questions.question_text: In adults, the spinal cord normally ends at: (DEP BOOK).
questions.check_explanation: In adults the conus medullaris typically terminates at the lower border of the L1 vertebra (often L1-L2 level).

check_why_others_wrong.b: L3 is below the usual termination level.
check_why_others_wrong.c: S1 is far below the conus medullaris.
check_why_others_wrong.d: L5 is also below the typical termination point.

questions.question_text: Regarding the spinal meninges, one of the following is true: (DEP BOOK).

options.label: a
options.text: The spinal arachnoid matter ends at the level of L2.

options.label: b
options.text: The spinal arteries lie in the epidural space.

options.label: c
options.text: The lower part of the spinal dura forms a sheath around the filum terminale.

options.label: d
options.text: The lumbar cistern extends from L1 to S3.

questions.check_explanation: The dura mater extends caudally as a sheath that encloses the filum terminale, forming the lower part of the dural sac.

check_why_others_wrong.a: Arachnoid mater extends to about S2, not L2.
check_why_others_wrong.b: Spinal arteries run in the subarachnoid space, not the epidural space.
check_why_others_wrong.d: The lumbar cistern typically extends from around L2 to S2, not L1 to S3.

questions.question_text: Regarding the blood supply of the spinal cord, one of the following is true: (DEP BOOK).

options.label: a
options.text: The posterior spinal artery supplies the anterior and lateral funiculi of the white matter.

options.label: b
options.text: The arteria radicularis magna supplies the cervical enlargement.

options.label: c
options.text: The internal vertebral venous plexus lies in the subdural space.

options.label: d
options.text: The thoracic region of the spinal cord is more liable.

questions.check_explanation: The thoracic spinal cord is a watershed area with relatively poor arterial supply, making it most vulnerable to ischemia.

check_why_others_wrong.a: Posterior spinal arteries supply dorsal columns, not anterior/lateral funiculi.
check_why_others_wrong.b: The artery of Adamkiewicz supplies the lumbar (lower thoracic) enlargement, not the cervical.
check_why_others_wrong.c: The internal vertebral venous plexus lies in the epidural space, not subdural.

questions.question_text: Regarding the meninges of the spinal cord, one of the following is true: (DEP BOOK).

options.label: a
options.text: The dura mater ends at the level of the third piece of sacrum.

options.label: b
options.text: The arachnoid mater ends at the level of the forth piece of sacrum.

options.label: c
options.text: The pia mater forms ligamentum denticulatum.

options.label: d
options.text: The subdural space contains the vertebral venous plexuses.

questions.check_explanation: The denticulate (ligamentum denticulatum) is formed by extensions of the pia mater that anchor the spinal cord to the dura.

check_why_others_wrong.a: Dura mater ends around S2, not S3.
check_why_others_wrong.b: Arachnoid mater ends around S2, not S4.
check_why_others_wrong.d: Vertebral venous plexus lies in the epidural space, not subdural.

questions.question_text: Regarding the spinal cord, one of the following is true: (DEP BOOK).

options.label: a
options.text: The spinal dura ends at the level of S4.

options.label: b
options.text: It is drained by spinal and vertebral venous plexuses.

options.label: d
options.text: The largest radicular artery is that of S2.

questions.check_explanation: The spinal cord venous blood drains into both the internal (spinal) and external (vertebral) venous plexuses.

check_why_others_wrong.a: The dural sac ends at S2, not S4.
check_why_others_wrong.c: The spinal cord has two, not three, enlargements.
check_why_others_wrong.d: The largest radicular artery is the artery of Adamkiewicz, not the S2 radicular artery.

questions.question_text: The lower end of spinal cord is called: (DEP BOOK).
questions.check_explanation: The tapered terminal portion of the spinal cord is the conus medullaris.

check_why_others_wrong.a: Cauda equina is the nerve roots below the conus, not the cord itself.
check_why_others_wrong.b: Denticulate ligament is a pia mater extension, not the cord end.
check_why_others_wrong.d: Option is garbled and not a recognized anatomical term.

questions.question_text: Substantia gelatinosa of Rolandi forms the second order neurons in the pathway of: (DEP BOOK).
questions.check_explanation: The substantia gelatinosa (Rexed lamina II) contains interneurons that become the second‑order neurons for both nociceptive (pain) and thermal (temperature) afferents in the spinothalamic pathway.

check_why_others_wrong.a: Pain is transmitted but temperature is also processed there.
check_why_others_wrong.b: Temperature is transmitted but pain is also processed there.
check_why_others_wrong.d: Simple touch ascends via the dorsal column, not the substantia gelatinosa.

questions.question_text: The posterior funiculus of the spinal cord contains: (DEP BOOK).

options.label: c
options.text: Both long ascending and descending fibers.

questions.check_explanation: The posterior (dorsal) funiculus contains the gracile and cuneate fasciculi, which are long ascending sensory tracts.

check_why_others_wrong.a: Descending fibers are located in the anterior and lateral funiculi, not posterior.
check_why_others_wrong.c: Only ascending, not descending, fibers are present in the posterior funiculus.
check_why_others_wrong.d: Associative (propriospinal) fibers are short intersegmental tracts, not the main component of the posterior funiculus.

questions.question_text: Regarding the pyramidal tract choose the correct answer: (DEP BOOK).

options.label: b
options.text: It arises only from the pyramidal cells of area 4 of the cerebral cortex.

options.label: c
options.text: About 15 % of its fibers normally form the pyramidal decussation.

options.label: d
options.text: It has a corticospinal and corticonuclear parts.

questions.check_explanation: The pyramidal tract comprises the corticospinal (to spinal cord) and corticobulbar (corticonuclear) components.

check_why_others_wrong.a: It is a bundle of axons from upper motor neurons, not a series of many neurons.
check_why_others_wrong.b: Originates also from premotor and supplementary motor areas, not only area 4.
check_why_others_wrong.c: Approximately 85‑90% of fibers cross at the pyramidal decussation, not ~15%.

questions.question_text: Regarding Brown Sequard syndrome; choose one best answer: (DEP BOOK).

options.label: a
options.text: It is associated with loss of reflexes at the level of the lesion.

options.label: b
options.text: It is usually associated with injury to nerve roots entering the segments below the lesion.

options.label: c
options.text: There is pyramidal tract lesion on the opposite side and proprioceptive lesion on the same side.

options.label: d
options.text: It is associated with loss of reflexes below the lesion.

questions.check_explanation: Brown-Sequard syndrome causes loss of reflexes at the level of the hemisection due to spinal shock, while reflexes below become hyperactive.

check_why_others_wrong.b: Nerve root injury is not a feature of the syndrome.
check_why_others_wrong.c: Both pyramidal and proprioceptive deficits are ipsilateral, not opposite.
check_why_others_wrong.d: Reflexes are increased, not lost, below the lesion.

questions.question_text: Regarding the blood supply to the spinal cord, select the correct statement: (DEP BOOK).

options.label: a
options.text: Anterior 2/3 of the spinal cord is supplied by the posterior spinal arteries.

options.label: b
options.text: Anterior spinal arteries are reinforced in the cervical region by branches from the vertebral arteries.

options.label: c
options.text: There are two anterior spinal arteries.

options.label: d
options.text: The cervical region of the spinal cord is predisposed to vascular insufficiency.

questions.check_explanation: The anterior spinal artery is formed by and reinforced in the cervical region by branches of the vertebral arteries.

check_why_others_wrong.a: Anterior 2/3 is supplied by the anterior spinal artery, not posterior arteries.
check_why_others_wrong.c: There is a single anterior spinal artery, not two.
check_why_others_wrong.d: The cervical cord has good collateral supply and is not the region most prone to ischemia.

questions.question_text: Regarding the spinal meninges select the correct statement: (DEP BOOK).

options.label: a
options.text: The denticulate ligament attaches pia to the arachnoid mater.

options.label: b
options.text: The pia mater is attached to the foramen magnum.

options.label: c
options.text: The arachnoid mater ends at L2 level.

options.label: d
options.text: The dura mater sends sheaths around the spinal nerve roots.

questions.check_explanation: The dura mater forms dural sleeves that extend around each spinal nerve root as it exits the vertebral canal.

check_why_others_wrong.a: Denticulate ligament connects pia to dura, not arachnoid.
check_why_others_wrong.b: Pia mater is not attached to the foramen magnum; dura is.
check_why_others_wrong.c: Arachnoid mater (and subarachnoid space) extend to about S2, not L2.

questions.question_text: Regarding the spinal meninges, select the true statement: (2019).

options.label: a
options.text: The denticulate ligaments are thickening of the dura mater.

options.label: b
options.text: The dura mater continues below as the film terminale.

options.label: c
options.text: The pia matter is closely adherent to the spinal cord.

options.label: d
options.text: The dura mater ends at the level of the fourth sacral vertebra.

questions.check_explanation: The pia mater is a delicate membrane that is tightly adherent to the surface of the spinal cord.

check_why_others_wrong.a: Denticulate ligaments are extensions of pia mater, not dura mater.
check_why_others_wrong.b: The filum terminale is a continuation of pia mater, not dura mater.
check_why_others_wrong.d: The dural sac ends at the level of S2, not S4.

questions.question_text: In performing a lumbar puncture for CSF collection, the needle Is Inserted Into: (2021 – 2023 - IPKA).
questions.check_explanation: Lumbar puncture accesses the subarachnoid space where cerebrospinal fluid circulates.

check_why_others_wrong.a: Subdural space lies between dura and arachnoid, not the CSF compartment.
check_why_others_wrong.b: Epidural (extradural) space is outside the dura and contains fat and veins, not CSF.
check_why_others_wrong.d: Extradural is synonymous with epidural, also outside the dura.

questions.question_text: The pyramidal tract lies in the midbrain in one of the following parts: (2018).
questions.check_explanation: In the midbrain the corticospinal (pyramidal) fibers occupy the middle third of the crus cerebri.

check_why_others_wrong.a: Too medial, only the most medial fibers are not the pyramidal tract.
check_why_others_wrong.b: Too lateral, the lateral edge contains frontopontine fibers.
check_why_others_wrong.d: Dorsal to the crus cerebri is not within the peduncle where the tract runs.

questions.question_text: A 50-year-old patient came to outpatient clinic. On examination, the physician found that there was a hemiplegia on the left side and medial squint on the right side. What are structures most likely affected? (2018).

options.label: a
options.text: Left pyramidal tract and left abducent nerve.

options.label: b
options.text: Right pyramidal tract and right abducent nerve.

options.label: c
options.text: Left pyramidal tract and left oculomotor nerve.

options.label: d
options.text: Right pyramidal tract and right oculomotor nerve.

questions.check_explanation: A right pyramidal tract lesion causes left-sided hemiplegia, and a right abducens (abducent) nerve lesion causes a medial deviation (squint) of the right eye.

check_why_others_wrong.a: Left pyramidal tract would cause right hemiplegia, not left.
check_why_others_wrong.c: Oculomotor nerve palsy causes eye down-and-out, not medial squint.
check_why_others_wrong.d: Oculomotor nerve palsy does not produce medial squint.

questions.question_text: The medial medullary syndrome (Dejerine syndrome) is characterized by: (2018).

options.label: b
options.text: Ipsilateral hemiplegia with contralateral hypoglossal paralysis.

options.label: c
options.text: Ipsilateral hypoglossal paralysis with contralateral hemiplegia.

questions.check_explanation: Medial medullary syndrome causes contralateral hemiplegia (corticospinal tract) and ipsilateral hypoglossal nerve palsy.

check_why_others_wrong.a: Hemiplegia is contralateral, not ipsilateral.
check_why_others_wrong.b: Both sides are reversed; hemiplegia is not ipsilateral.
check_why_others_wrong.d: Hypoglossal palsy is ipsilateral, not contralateral.

questions.question_text: Patient came to ER with LMNL of the hypoglossal nerve on the right side and UMNL hemiplegia on the left side. Where is the site of the lesion? (2017).
questions.check_explanation: A right‑sided medullary lesion can involve the hypoglossal nucleus (producing right LMN tongue palsy) and the corticospinal tract after it has crossed, giving left UMN hemiplegia.

check_why_others_wrong.a: Motor cortex lesion gives only UMN signs, no hypoglossal LMN involvement.
check_why_others_wrong.b: Midbrain lesions affect cranial nerves III–IV, not the hypoglossal nerve.
check_why_others_wrong.c: Pons lesions involve facial and other pontine nuclei, not the hypoglossal nucleus.

questions.question_text: The pyramidal tract fibers supply the following cranial nerve nucleus: (2017).
questions.check_explanation: Pyramidal (corticobulbar) fibers innervate motor nuclei of cranial nerves, including the trigeminal motor nucleus, whereas the other listed nuclei are purely sensory.

check_why_others_wrong.a: Olfactory nucleus is sensory only, no pyramidal input.
check_why_others_wrong.b: Optic nucleus is sensory (retina), not supplied by pyramidal fibers.
check_why_others_wrong.d: Vestibulocochlear nucleus is sensory, not a target of pyramidal tract.

questions.question_text: The following artery shares in the supply of the medulla: (2016).
questions.check_explanation: The posterior inferior cerebellar artery (PICA), a branch of the vertebral artery, supplies the lateral medulla.

check_why_others_wrong.b: Supplies the superior cerebellum, not the medulla.
check_why_others_wrong.c: Supplies occipital and inferior temporal lobes, not the medulla.
check_why_others_wrong.d: Supplies the cerebral hemispheres, not the medulla.

questions.question_text: Which of the following cranial nerves exits the posterior aspect of the brainstem? One of the following cranial nerves is attached to the posterior aspect of the brain stem: (DEP BOOK - 2024).
questions.check_explanation: The trochlear nerve (IV) is the only cranial nerve that emerges from the dorsal (posterior) surface of the brainstem.

check_why_others_wrong.a: Abducens exits ventrally from the pons.
check_why_others_wrong.b: Hypoglossal exits ventrally from the medulla.
check_why_others_wrong.c: Trigeminal exits laterally from the pons.
check_why_others_wrong.e: Oculomotor exits ventrally from the midbrain.
check_why_others_wrong.f: Vagus exits laterally from the medulla.

questions.question_text: 50-year-old patient came to outpatient clinic. On examination, the physician found that there was a hemiplegia on the left side and medial squint on the right side. What are structures most likely affected? (2017).

options.label: a
options.text: Left pyramidal tract and left abducent nerve.

options.label: b
options.text: Right pyramidal tract and right abducent nerve.

options.label: c
options.text: Left pyramidal tract and left oculomotor nerve.

options.label: d
options.text: Right pyramidal tract and right oculomotor nerve.

questions.check_explanation: Left hemiplegia indicates a lesion of the contralateral (right) pyramidal tract; a right medial squint results from right abducens (lateral rectus) palsy, causing unopposed medial rectus pull.

check_why_others_wrong.a: Would cause right hemiplegia and left medial squint, opposite of findings.
check_why_others_wrong.c: Oculomotor palsy causes eye deviation outward and down, not medial squint.
check_why_others_wrong.d: Combines right pyramidal lesion (correct) with oculomotor palsy, which does not produce medial squint.

questions.question_text: In case of right corticonuclear tract injury above the level of the motor nucleus of. facial nerve, which side of the face is affected? (2017).
questions.check_explanation: A right corticobulbar lesion above the facial nucleus spares the upper face (bilateral input) and paralyzes the contralateral lower face, i.e., the left lower half.

check_why_others_wrong.a: Upper face is bilaterally innervated, not affected on the right.
check_why_others_wrong.b: Lower face receives contralateral input, so right lesion affects left side.
check_why_others_wrong.c: Upper face is spared due to bilateral cortical supply.

questions.question_text: Facial colliculus overlies (2015).
questions.check_explanation: The facial colliculus is a raised area on the dorsal pons formed by facial nerve fibers looping over the abducens (abducent) nucleus, so it overlies that nucleus.

check_why_others_wrong.b: Facial motor nucleus lies ventrally in the pons, not beneath the facial colliculus.
check_why_others_wrong.c: Hypoglossal nucleus is located in the medulla, far from the facial colliculus.
check_why_others_wrong.d: Dorsal nucleus of X is also in the medulla, not under the facial colliculus.
check_why_others_wrong.e: Cochlear nuclei are lateral at the pontomedullary junction, not beneath the facial colliculus.

questions.question_text: Concerning the olive, select the correct statement: (DEP BOOK).

options.label: a
options.text: Lies between the median and anterolateral fissures.

options.label: b
options.text: Is related posteriorly to the rootlets of hypoglossal nerve.

options.label: c
options.text: Is related posteriorly to the rootlets of 9, 10 and 11 cranial nerves.

options.label: d
options.text: Is produced by the superior olivary nucleus.

questions.check_explanation: No option correctly describes the anatomical position or origin of the inferior olivary nucleus.

check_why_others_wrong.a: Olive lies lateral to the anterolateral sulcus, not between median and anterolateral fissures
check_why_others_wrong.b: Olive is lateral, not posterior, to the hypoglossal rootlets
check_why_others_wrong.c: Olive is anterior to the IX, X, XI rootlets, not posterior
check_why_others_wrong.d: Olive is not produced by the superior olivary nucleus

questions.question_text: Regarding the olive, one of the following is incorrect: (2021 - IPKA).

options.label: a
options.text: Lies on the lateral surface of medulla oblongata.

options.label: a

options.label: b
options.text: The primary fissure present on its lower surface.

questions.question_text: Regarding the cerebellum, one of the following is true: (DEP BOOK).

options.label: a
options.text: The neocerebellum consists of the flocculonodular lobe.

questions.question_text: One of the following is part of inferior vermis: (DEP BOOK).

check_why_others_wrong.b: Declive is part of the superior vermis.
check_why_others_wrong.c: Folium vermis is located in the superior/posterior vermis, not the inferior.

questions.question_text: Concerning the cerebellum; choose the most correct answer: (DEP BOOK).

options.label: a
options.text: Related to the mastoid air cells.

check_why_others_wrong.c: The cerebellum is part of the hindbrain (metencephalon), not the forebrain.
check_why_others_wrong.d: The cerebellum is related to the fourth ventricle, not the third ventricle.

questions.question_text: Select the correct statement about the cerebellum: (DEP BOOK).

options.label: a
options.text: The cerebellum has two surfaces; upper and lower.

options.label: b

options.label: c
options.text: The anterior notch is occupied by the falx cerebrii.

options.text: The flocculus is a small part of the cerebral hemisphere.

questions.check_explanation: The cerebellum is described as having a superior (upper) and an inferior (lower) surface.

check_why_others_wrong.b: Cerebellum has three lobes, not two.

check_why_others_wrong.d: The flocculus is a part of the cerebellum, not the cerebral hemisphere.

questions.question_text: The central canal of the spinal cord opens out into the: (2019).

check_why_others_wrong.a: The subarachnoid space surrounds the cord but is not a continuation of the central canal.
check_why_others_wrong.b: The lumbar cistern is a subarachnoid space enlargement, not connected to the central canal.

questions.question_text: The choroid plexus of the 4th ventricle is derived from the following artery: (2017).
questions.check_explanation: The choroid plexus of the fourth ventricle is primarily supplied by branches of the posterior inferior cerebellar artery (PICA).

check_why_others_wrong.b: AICA supplies lateral pons and inner ear, not the fourth-ventricle choroid plexus.
check_why_others_wrong.c: Superior cerebellar artery supplies the superior cerebellum, not the choroid plexus.
check_why_others_wrong.d: Middle cerebral artery supplies the cerebral hemispheres, not the fourth ventricle.

questions.question_text: The MRI of an 11-year-old boy shows a tumor in the pontine portion of the fourth ventricle. The rostral edge of which of the following structures represents the border between the medullary and pontine parts of the fourth ventricle? (DEP BOOK).
questions.check_explanation: The stria medullaris runs horizontally across the floor of the fourth ventricle; its rostral edge marks the transition between the pontine (superior) and medullary (inferior) portions.

check_why_others_wrong.a: Facial colliculus is a pontine floor landmark, not the dividing line.
check_why_others_wrong.b: Hypoglossal trigone lies in the medullary (inferior) part, not at the border.
check_why_others_wrong.c: Medial eminence is a midline elevation present throughout, not a boundary marker.

questions.question_text: Concerning the 4th ventricle, select the correct statement: (DEP BOOK).

check_why_others_wrong.a: Floor is formed by the dorsal medulla and pons, not described accurately.

questions.question_text: One of the following cranial nerve nuclei is not present in the floor of the 4th ventricle: (2021).

options.text: Dorsal motor nucleus of the vagus.

questions.check_explanation: The oculomotor nucleus lies in the midbrain, not on the floor (rhomboid fossa) of the fourth ventricle.

check_why_others_wrong.a: Abducens nucleus is located in the dorsal pons on the floor of the fourth ventricle.
check_why_others_wrong.c: Dorsal motor nucleus of the vagus is situated in the medulla on the floor of the fourth ventricle.
check_why_others_wrong.d: Hypoglossal nucleus is found in the medulla on the floor of the fourth ventricle.

questions.question_text: Foramen of Luschka connects the: (2021).

questions.question_text: Concerning the fourth ventricle; choose the correct answer: (2019 – DEP BOOK).

options.text: Its floor is formed by the closed medulla and pons.

options.label: b
options.text: Its roof is formed by the superior and inferior medullary vela.

questions.check_explanation: The roof of the fourth ventricle is formed by the superior and inferior medullary vela (laminae).

check_why_others_wrong.a: Floor is formed by the dorsal surfaces of the pons and medulla, not a 'closed' structure.
check_why_others_wrong.c: The choroid plexus lies in the roof (tela choroidea), not the floor.

questions.question_text: The upper angle of 4th ventricle communicates it with: (IPKA).
questions.check_explanation: The upper (superior) angle of the fourth ventricle is continuous with the cerebral aqueduct (aqueduct of Sylvius) that links the third and fourth ventricles.

check_why_others_wrong.b: The central canal runs within the spinal cord, not directly from the fourth ventricle.
check_why_others_wrong.c: The foramen of Magendie is the median aperture at the lower part of the fourth ventricle.
check_why_others_wrong.d: The foramen of Monro connects the lateral ventricles to the third ventricle, not the fourth.

questions.question_text: A foramen that connects the 4th ventricle with the subarachnoid space: (IPKA).
questions.check_explanation: The median aperture (foramen of Magendie) is the opening that allows CSF to flow from the fourth ventricle into the subarachnoid space.

check_why_others_wrong.a: Central canal of midbrain is an internal canal, not an external foramen.
check_why_others_wrong.c: Interventricular (foramen of Monro) connects lateral ventricles to the third ventricle.
check_why_others_wrong.d: Central canal of medulla is an internal canal, not a connection to the subarachnoid space.

questions.question_text: The roof of the 4th ventricle is formed by: (2023).
questions.check_explanation: The dorsal roof of the fourth ventricle is formed by the cerebellar vermis and hemispheres.

check_why_others_wrong.b: Corpus callosum forms roof of lateral ventricles, not fourth.
check_why_others_wrong.c: Tectum is a midbrain structure, unrelated to fourth ventricle roof.
check_why_others_wrong.d: Thalamus contributes to lateral ventricle walls, not fourth ventricle roof.

questions.question_text: Which ventricle lies between the pons and cerebellum? (2024).
questions.check_explanation: The fourth ventricle is located in the dorsal brainstem, bounded anteriorly by the pons and posteriorly by the cerebellum.

check_why_others_wrong.a: Lateral ventricles are in the cerebral hemispheres, not near the pons.
check_why_others_wrong.b: Third ventricle lies between the thalami, not between pons and cerebellum.
check_why_others_wrong.d: A 'fifth ventricle' is not a recognized ventricle in standard neuroanatomy.

questions.question_text: Concerning the fourth ventricle; choose the most correct answer. (DEP BOOK).

check_why_others_wrong.c: Choroid plexus lies in the roof, not the floor.

check_why_others_wrong.a: Fourth ventricle belongs to the hindbrain, not telencephalon.

questions.question_text: One of the following is incorrect concerning the insula: (2021).

options.label: a
options.text: It is a conical mass of grey mater lying in the depth of the lateral sulcus.

options.label: b
options.text: It is surrounded by a circular sulcus.

options.label: c
options.text: Its apex is referred to as the pulvinar.

options.label: d
options.text: Has three opercula, frontal, parietal and temporal.

check_why_others_wrong.b: Correct; the insula is encircled by the circular sulcus.
check_why_others_wrong.d: Correct; the insula is covered by frontal, parietal and temporal opercula.

questions.question_text: One of the opercula of the insula is: (2020).
questions.check_explanation: The insula is covered by opercula from the frontal, parietal, and temporal lobes; the temporal operculum is one of them.

check_why_others_wrong.b: Occipital lobe does not form an operculum over the insula.
check_why_others_wrong.c: Infundibular refers to hypothalamic region, not an operculum.
check_why_others_wrong.d: Parahippocampal gyrus is medial temporal, not an operculum covering the insula.

questions.question_text: Insula is a part of the cerebral cortex hidden within the depth of: (2019).
questions.check_explanation: The insular cortex lies deep within the Sylvian (lateral) sulcus, specifically in the region of its posterior ramus.

check_why_others_wrong.b: Central sulcus separates frontal and parietal lobes, not the insula.
check_why_others_wrong.c: Superior temporal sulcus is lateral to the temporal lobe, not the insular region.
check_why_others_wrong.d: Intraparietal sulcus is located in the parietal lobe, unrelated to the insula.

questions.question_text: One of the following gyri is not visible on the medial surface: (2023).

check_why_others_wrong.a: Lingual gyrus forms part of the medial occipital surface.
check_why_others_wrong.b: Callosal region (gyrus adjacent to the corpus callosum) is on the medial surface.
check_why_others_wrong.c: Cingulate gyrus is a prominent medial cortical ridge.

questions.question_text: One of the following sulci is on the medial surface of the cerebral hemisphere: (2023).
questions.check_explanation: The cingulate sulcus runs on the medial surface above the cingulate gyrus, whereas the other sulci are located on the lateral surface.

check_why_others_wrong.b: Central sulcus is on the lateral surface separating frontal and parietal lobes.
check_why_others_wrong.c: Superior temporal sulcus lies on the lateral surface of the temporal lobe.
check_why_others_wrong.d: Posterior ramus of the lateral sulcus is also on the lateral surface.

check_why_others_wrong.b: Gyrus rectus lies medial, not lateral, to the olfactory sulcus.
check_why_others_wrong.c: The orbital surface rests on the orbital plate of the frontal bone, not the tentorium cerebelli.
check_why_others_wrong.d: Only the olfactory tract, not the bulb, is on the orbital surface.

questions.question_text: Regarding the cingulate sulcus; choose one best answer: (DEP BOOK).

questions.check_explanation: The cingulate sulcus originates anteriorly on the medial surface, just above the rostrum of the corpus callosum.

check_why_others_wrong.c: The terminal branches are the marginal and subparietal sulci; the terms submarginal and parietal are inaccurate.

questions.question_text: The cingulum: (DEP BOOK).

options.label: a
options.text: Connects the orbital gyri of the frontal lobe with the anterior part of the temporal lobe.

options.label: b
options.text: Makes arch over the stem of the lateral sulcus.

options.label: d
options.text: Supplied by the anterior cerebral artery.

questions.check_explanation: The cingulum lies within the cingulate gyrus and receives its blood supply from the pericallosal branch of the anterior cerebral artery.

check_why_others_wrong.a: It connects the cingulate gyrus to the parahippocampal gyrus, not specifically the orbital gyri.
check_why_others_wrong.b: It does not arch over the lateral sulcus; that region belongs to the insula.
check_why_others_wrong.c: The tract follows a smooth curve, not a sharp bend.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a part of the hypothalamus? (2019).
questions.check_explanation: Mammillary bodies are nuclei located in the posterior hypothalamus.

check_why_others_wrong.a: Pineal body belongs to the epithalamus, not hypothalamus.
check_why_others_wrong.b: Medial geniculate body is a thalamic auditory nucleus.
check_why_others_wrong.c: Anterior commissure is a fiber tract, not a hypothalamic structure.

questions.question_text: One of the following structures is not a content of the interpeduncular fossa: (2017).

check_why_others_wrong.c: The infundibulum (pituitary stalk) passes through the fossa.
check_why_others_wrong.d: The tuber cinereum is a hypothalamic region within the fossa.

questions.question_text: One of the following structures is a content of the interpeduncular fossa: (2015).
questions.check_explanation: The posterior perforated substance lies in the interpeduncular fossa, containing perforating branches of the posterior cerebral artery.

check_why_others_wrong.a: Lamina terminalis forms the anterior wall of the third ventricle, not in the fossa.
check_why_others_wrong.c: Anterior perforated substance is located anterior to the optic chiasm, not within the interpeduncular fossa.
check_why_others_wrong.d: Olive is a structure of the medulla oblongata.
check_why_others_wrong.e: Optic tract runs lateral to the hypothalamus, not in the interpeduncular fossa.

questions.question_text: One of the following is not a content of the interpeduncular fossa:  (2021 – IPKA - 2023).

check_why_others_wrong.a: Tuber cinereum forms part of the floor of the interpeduncular fossa.
check_why_others_wrong.b: Mammillary bodies lie at the posterior wall of the fossa.
check_why_others_wrong.c: Posterior perforated substance is the central floor of the fossa.

questions.question_text: The interpeduncular fossa contain: (2019).
questions.check_explanation: The mammillary bodies lie on the ventral surface of the diencephalon within the interpeduncular fossa between the cerebral peduncles.

check_why_others_wrong.a: Anterior perforated substance is on the basal surface of the cerebral hemispheres, not in the interpeduncular fossa.
check_why_others_wrong.c: Pineal stalk is dorsal in the quadrigeminal region, not in the interpeduncular fossa.
check_why_others_wrong.d: Tuber vermis is part of the cerebellum, located posteriorly, not in the interpeduncular fossa.

questions.question_text: The cranial nerve that emerge from the interpeduncular fossa around medial aspect of the cerebral peduncle is: (2023).
questions.check_explanation: The oculomotor nerve (CN III) exits the midbrain in the interpeduncular fossa between the cerebral peduncles.

check_why_others_wrong.b: CN IV emerges dorsally from the inferior colliculus, not the interpeduncular fossa.
check_why_others_wrong.c: CN V originates from the pons, not the interpeduncular fossa.
check_why_others_wrong.d: CN VI arises at the pontomedullary junction, not the interpeduncular fossa.

questions.question_text: One of the following structures is a content of interpeduncular fossa: (DEP BOOK).
questions.check_explanation: The mammillary bodies form the posterior wall of the interpeduncular fossa, making them a content of this depression.

check_why_others_wrong.b: Tuberculum cinereum lies rostral to the interpeduncular fossa, not within it.
check_why_others_wrong.c: Anterior perforated substance is on the basal forebrain, anterior to the fossa.
check_why_others_wrong.d: Optic tract runs lateral to the hypothalamus, not in the interpeduncular fossa.

questions.question_text: Concerning the interpeduncular fossa, one of the following is a boundary of the fossa: (DEP BOOK).

check_why_others_wrong.c: The optic nerve lies anterior to the chiasm, not at the fossa.

questions.question_text: One of the following is correct: (DEP BOOK).

questions.question_text: One of the following does not belong to the long association fibers: (2019).

check_why_others_wrong.a: Cingulum is an association fiber of the limbic system.
check_why_others_wrong.b: Uncinate fasciculus is an association fiber linking frontal and temporal lobes.
check_why_others_wrong.c: Superior longitudinal bundle is an association fiber connecting frontal, parietal, occipital lobes.
check_why_others_wrong.e: Inferior longitudinal bundle is an association fiber linking occipital and temporal lobes.

questions.question_text: Regarding the internal capsule, the auditory radiation passes in: (2019 - 2018).

check_why_others_wrong.d: Anterior choroidal artery supplies the posterior limb.

questions.question_text: The greatest commissure in the brain is: (2018).
questions.check_explanation: The corpus callosum is the largest interhemispheric commissure, linking the two cerebral hemispheres.

check_why_others_wrong.a: Habenular commissure is tiny, connecting the habenular nuclei.
check_why_others_wrong.b: Hippocampal (commissure of fornix) is much smaller.

questions.question_text: The following are projection fibers of the cerebral hemisphere: (2017).

check_why_others_wrong.b: Cingulum is an association fiber within the limbic system.

check_why_others_wrong.c: The infundibular recess is a downward extension of the third ventricle containing the pituitary stalk.

questions.question_text: The 3rd ventricle is bounded anteriorly by: (2023).
questions.check_explanation: The third ventricle is a narrow, midline cavity bounded anteriorly by the lamina terminalis, which connects the two foramina of Monro.

check_why_others_wrong.a: The pineal body is located posteriorly, associated with the posterior wall and the quadrigeminal plate.
check_why_others_wrong.b: The subthalamus forms part of the lateral wall of the third ventricle.
check_why_others_wrong.d: The habenular commissure is located on the posterior wall of the third ventricle.

questions.question_text: The following statements concern the third ventricle, one of them is correct: (2024).

options.label: a
options.text: It is the cavity of the hindbrain.

options.label: b
options.text: It communicates with the lateral ventricles through the cerebral aqueduct.

options.label: c
options.text: It is continuous with the fourth ventricle through the interventricular foramen.

options.label: d
options.text: The choroid plexus is located in the roof.

questions.check_explanation: The third ventricle is a midline cavity in the diencephalon (interbrain), not the hindbrain. It communicates with the lateral ventricles via the interventricular foramina (of Monro) and with the fourth ventricle via the cerebral aqueduct. The choroid plexus is located in the roof of the third ventricle (specifically the tela choroidea).

check_why_others_wrong.a: The third ventricle is part of the diencephalon, not the hindbrain.
check_why_others_wrong.b: It communicates with lateral ventricles via the interventricular foramina, not the cerebral aqueduct.
check_why_others_wrong.c: It communicates with the fourth ventricle via the cerebral aqueduct, not the interventricular foramen.
