check_why_others_wrong.a: The third ventricle is part of the diencephalon, not the hindbrain.
check_why_others_wrong.b: It communicates with lateral ventricles via the interventricular foramina, not the cerebral aqueduct.
check_why_others_wrong.c: It communicates with the fourth ventricle via the cerebral aqueduct, not the interventricular foramen.

questions.question_text: The cisterna magna of subarachnoid space is a name given to the: (2019).
questions.check_explanation: The cisterna magna, also called the cerebellomedullary cistern, lies between the cerebellum and the medulla in the subarachnoid space.

check_why_others_wrong.a: Interpeduncular cistern is located between the cerebral peduncles, not posterior to the cerebellum.
check_why_others_wrong.b: Cistern of the corpus callosum (cavernous cistern) is anterior, above the corpus callosum.
check_why_others_wrong.c: Cistern of the lateral fissure (Sylvian cistern) is in the lateral sulcus, not the posterior fossa.

questions.question_text: Which statement about the meninges is most accurate? (DEP BOOK).

options.label: a
options.text: Dura mater has two distinct layers surrounding brain and spinal cord.

options.label: b
options.text: The major venous sinuses lie in the subdural space.

options.label: c
options.text: Rupture of middle meningeal artery causes subarachnoid hemorrhage.

options.label: d
options.text: Dura mater is thickened either side of the spinal cord to form the denticulate ligaments.

options.label: e
options.text: Pia mater pierces the distal extreme of the dura as the filum terminale.

questions.check_explanation: The pia mater extends inferiorly from the conus medullaris to form the filum terminale, which pierces the dural sac to attach to the coccyx. The other options contain factual errors regarding meningeal layers, sinus location, hemorrhage types, or ligament origin.

check_why_others_wrong.a: The dura mater has two distinct layers (periosteal and meningeal) only in the cranial cavity; in the spinal canal, it is a single layer.
check_why_others_wrong.b: The major venous sinuses (e.g., superior sagittal sinus) lie in the subdural space? No, they lie between the two layers of the dura mater (dural venous sinuses), not in the subdural space.
check_why_others_wrong.c: Rupture of the middle meningeal artery causes an epidural (extradural) hematoma, not a subarachnoid hemorrhage.
check_why_others_wrong.d: The denticulate ligaments are formed by thickenings of the pia mater, not the dura mater.

questions.question_text: The cisterna magna of the subarachnoid space is a name given to the: (2021 - 2024).
questions.check_explanation: The cisterna magna is the large subarachnoid space located between the posterior surface of the cerebellum and the dorsal surface of the medulla oblongata, also known as the cerebello-medullary cistern.

check_why_others_wrong.b: The interpeduncular cistern is located between the cerebral peduncles of the midbrain.
check_why_others_wrong.c: The cistern of the lateral fissure (Sylvian cistern) is located in the lateral sulcus.
check_why_others_wrong.d: The pontine cistern is located anterior to the pons.

questions.question_text: Which part of the ventricular system contains the choroid plexus: (2020).
questions.check_explanation: The choroid plexus is located in the roof of the third ventricle (specifically the tela choroidea), as well as in the bodies of the lateral ventricles and the fourth ventricle. It is not present in the frontal or occipital horns of the lateral ventricles or the cerebral aqueduct.

check_why_others_wrong.a: The frontal horn of the lateral ventricle does not contain choroid plexus; the plexus is found in the body of the lateral ventricle.
check_why_others_wrong.b: The occipital horn of the lateral ventricle does not contain choroid plexus.
check_why_others_wrong.d: The cerebral aqueduct does not contain choroid plexus.

questions.question_text: Regarding cranial meninges, one of the following is true: (2019).

options.label: a
options.text: Outer layer of the dura forms dural folds to separate different parts of brain.

options.label: c
options.text: Extradural space is the space between the dura and arachnoid.

options.label: d
options.text: The dural fold between cerebral and cerebellar hemispheres is called falx cerebelli.

questions.check_explanation: The subarachnoid space is the potential space between the arachnoid mater and the pia mater, which is filled with cerebrospinal fluid (CSF).

check_why_others_wrong.a: The inner layer of the dura mater (meningeal layer) forms the dural folds (falx cerebri, falx cerebelli, tentorium cerebelli), not the outer (periosteal) layer.
check_why_others_wrong.c: The space between the dura and arachnoid is the subdural space; the extradural (epidural) space is between the dura and the skull.
check_why_others_wrong.d: The dural fold between the cerebral hemispheres is the falx cerebri; the falx cerebelli is a small fold within the posterior cranial fossa.

questions.question_text: Pia matter: (2024).

options.label: b
options.text: Is carried into all its sulci.

options.label: c
options.text: Bridges over the various sulci on the surface of the brain.

options.label: d
options.text: Its two layers enclose venous sinuses.

questions.check_explanation: The pia mater is a delicate, highly vascular membrane that closely adheres to the surface of the brain and extends into all sulci and fissures. In contrast, the dura mater is the tough outer membrane that bridges over the sulci and forms the venous sinuses between its layers.

check_why_others_wrong.a: The dura mater is the tough outer membrane; the pia mater is delicate and thin.
check_why_others_wrong.c: The dura mater bridges over the sulci; the pia mater dips into them.
check_why_others_wrong.d: The venous sinuses are located between the two layers of the dura mater (dural venous sinuses), not the pia mater.

questions.question_text: The cisterna magna of subarachnoid space is a name given to the: (DEP BOOK).
questions.check_explanation: The cisterna magna is the large subarachnoid cistern located between the cerebellum and the medulla oblongata, also known as the cerebellomedullary cistern.

check_why_others_wrong.a: The interpeduncular cistern is located between the cerebral peduncles in the midbrain region.
check_why_others_wrong.b: The cistern of the corpus callosum is located above the corpus callosum in the interhemispheric fissure.
check_why_others_wrong.c: The cistern of the lateral fissure (Sylvian cistern) is located within the lateral sulcus.

questions.question_text: Regarding meninges, one of the following is true: (DEP BOOK).

options.label: a
options.text: Inner layer of dura forms folds to separate different parts of brain.

options.label: b
options.text: Extradural space is between dura & arachnoid.

options.label: c
options.text: dura dips into the sulci of brains.

questions.check_explanation: The subarachnoid space is the potential space between the arachnoid mater and the pia mater, and it is filled with cerebrospinal fluid (CSF).

check_why_others_wrong.a: The inner layer of the dura (dura mater) forms the falx cerebri and tentorium cerebelli, which separate hemispheres or the cerebrum from the cerebellum, but the phrasing 'separate different parts of brain' is less precise than the definitive fact in D; however, D is the standard correct answer in this context.
check_why_others_wrong.b: The extradural (epidural) space is between the skull and the dura mater, not between the dura and arachnoid.
check_why_others_wrong.c: The dura mater does not dip into the sulci; the pia mater follows the contours of the brain, including the sulci.

questions.question_text: Concerning the arachnoid villi and granulations; choose one best answer: (DEP BOOK).

options.label: b
options.text: They are found in large numbers along the superior sagittal sinus.

questions.check_explanation: Arachnoid granulations are most numerous along the superior sagittal sinus, where they project into the dural venous sinuses to facilitate CSF absorption. They are known to erode or indent the inner table of the skull (creating granular foveolae), so option a is incorrect.

check_why_others_wrong.a: Arachnoid granulations frequently indent the inner table of the skull, creating visible impressions known as granular foveolae.
check_why_others_wrong.c: Arachnoid granulations typically increase in size and number with age, not in children.
check_why_others_wrong.d: Arachnoid granulations are involved in the absorption of CSF into the venous system, not its formation (which occurs in the choroid plexus).

questions.question_text: A 9-month-old infant presented with hydrocephalus (intracranial accumulation of CSF). What is the possible site of obstruction? (2018 - 2016).
questions.check_explanation: Obstruction at the foramina of Magendie and Luschka prevents CSF outflow from the fourth ventricle into the subarachnoid space, leading to hydrocephalus. This is a common cause of non-communicating hydrocephalus in infants.

check_why_others_wrong.b: The foramen caecum is a blind-ending structure in the nasal cavity, not part of the CSF circulation.
check_why_others_wrong.c: The central canal of the spinal cord is a small channel that does not obstruct CSF flow to cause hydrocephalus.
check_why_others_wrong.d: The '5th ventricle' is not a standard anatomical term for a CSF pathway; it may refer to the suprasellar cistern, but obstruction there is not the primary site for this presentation.

questions.question_text: The sites where cerebrospinal fluid passes from around the brain into the venous system is/are called: (2019).
questions.check_explanation: Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) drains from the subarachnoid space into the dural venous sinuses (specifically the superior sagittal sinus) via arachnoid villi (or arachnoid granulations).

check_why_others_wrong.a: Choroid plexuses are the sites of CSF production, not drainage.
check_why_others_wrong.b: Lateral apertures (foramina of Luschka) allow CSF to flow from the 4th ventricle into the subarachnoid space.
check_why_others_wrong.c: The median aperture (foramen of Magendie) allows CSF to flow from the 4th ventricle into the subarachnoid space.

questions.question_text: A 55-year-old male farmer was admitted to the emergency department after falling. from hayloft. Radiographic examination revealed a small, depressed fracture of the. skull vertex and thrombosis of the superior sagittal sinus. A day later, the patient lost. his consciousness. What is the most likely cause for his loss of consciousness? (2018).

options.label: b
options.text: Obstruction of the cerebral aqueduct of Sylvius.

options.label: c
options.text: Laceration of the middle meningeal artery.

options.label: d
options.text: Aneurysm of the middle cerebral artery.

questions.check_explanation: Thrombosis of the superior sagittal sinus obstructs the drainage of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) from the arachnoid granulations, leading to increased intracranial pressure and subsequent loss of consciousness.

check_why_others_wrong.b: The cerebral aqueduct connects the third and fourth ventricles and is not directly affected by superior sagittal sinus thrombosis.
check_why_others_wrong.c: Laceration of the middle meningeal artery causes an epidural hematoma, typically associated with temporal bone fractures, not vertex fractures or sinus thrombosis.
check_why_others_wrong.d: An aneurysm of the middle cerebral artery is a vascular pathology unrelated to the described trauma and sinus thrombosis.

questions.question_text: A 5-day-old infant was diagnosed with a noncommunicating hydrocephalus (intracranial accumulation of CSF). Which of the following is most likely to lead to such a condition? (2015).

options.label: a
options.text: Obstruction in the circulation of the cerebrospinal fluid.

options.label: c
options.text: Disturbances in the resorption of cerebrospinal fluid.

options.label: e
options.text: Failure of the neural tube to close.

questions.check_explanation: Noncommunicating (obstructive) hydrocephalus is defined by a physical blockage in the flow of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) within the ventricular system, such as at the foramen of Monro or aqueduct of Sylvius. This obstruction prevents CSF from circulating freely, leading to its accumulation.

check_why_others_wrong.b: Increased head size is a clinical sign/symptom of hydrocephalus, not the underlying cause.
check_why_others_wrong.c: Disturbances in resorption (e.g., arachnoid granulations) typically cause communicating hydrocephalus, where CSF can flow freely in the subarachnoid space.
check_why_others_wrong.d: Excess production is rare (e.g., choroid plexus papilloma) and is not the most common cause of noncommunicating hydrocephalus in infants.
check_why_others_wrong.e: Failure of the neural tube to close results in neural tube defects like spina bifida or anencephaly, not hydrocephalus.

questions.question_text: Regarding the ventricular system and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) production, which of the following statements is true? (DEP BOOK).

options.label: a
options.text: CSF is exclusively produced in the choroid plexi of the lateral ventricles.

options.label: b
options.text: CSF passes from the 3rd to the 4th ventricle via the interventricular foramen.

options.label: c
options.text: The 4th ventricle communicates directly with the subarachnoid space.

options.label: d
options.text: The total daily production of CSF is approximately 150 ml.

options.label: e
options.text: CSF is reabsorbed mainly through the arachnoid granulations in the. inferior sagittal sinus.

questions.check_explanation: The 4th ventricle communicates directly with the subarachnoid space via the median aperture (foramen of Magendie) and the lateral apertures (foramina of Luschka). CSF is produced in the choroid plexi of all four ventricles, not just the lateral ones. The passage from the 3rd to the 4th ventricle is via the cerebral aqueduct, not the interventricular foramen. Daily production is ~500 ml, and reabsorption occurs primarily in the superior sagittal sinus.

check_why_others_wrong.a: CSF is produced in the choroid plexi of the lateral, 3rd, and 4th ventricles, not exclusively the lateral ventricles.
check_why_others_wrong.b: CSF passes from the 3rd to the 4th ventricle via the cerebral aqueduct (aqueduct of Sylvius), not the interventricular foramen (which connects lateral to 3rd).
check_why_others_wrong.d: Total daily CSF production is approximately 500 ml, not 150 ml (150 ml is the total volume at any given time).
check_why_others_wrong.e: CSF is reabsorbed mainly through arachnoid granulations in the superior sagittal sinus, not the inferior sagittal sinus.

questions.question_text: Foramen of Luschka connects the: (2021).

options.label: a
options.text: Lateral ventricle with the third ventricle.

options.label: c
options.text: Third ventricle with the fourth ventricle.

options.label: d
options.text: Fourth ventricle with the subarachnoid space.

questions.check_explanation: The foramina of Luschka (lateral apertures) are openings in the lateral walls of the fourth ventricle that allow cerebrospinal fluid to flow into the subarachnoid space.

check_why_others_wrong.a: The interventricular foramen (of Monro) connects the lateral ventricles to the third ventricle.
check_why_others_wrong.b: The lateral ventricles are not directly connected to each other; they connect via the third ventricle.
check_why_others_wrong.c: The cerebral aqueduct (of Sylvius) connects the third ventricle to the fourth ventricle.

questions.question_text: One of the following is not true concerning the arachnoid granulations: (2021).

options.label: a
options.text: They are found along the superior sagittal sinus.

options.label: c
options.text: They consist of aggregation of arachnoid villi.

options.label: d
options.text: They indent the overlying skull bone in the old age.

questions.check_explanation: Arachnoid granulations are responsible for the reabsorption of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) into the venous sinuses, not its production. CSF is produced by the choroid plexus.

check_why_others_wrong.a: Arachnoid granulations are most commonly found projecting into the superior sagittal sinus.
check_why_others_wrong.c: They are formed by the aggregation of arachnoid villi.
check_why_others_wrong.d: In elderly individuals, the pressure from these granulations can cause indentations (granular impressions) in the inner table of the skull.

questions.question_text: Cerebrospinal fluid circulates through all of the following except: (2019).
questions.check_explanation: Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) circulates through the ventricular system (lateral, third, and fourth ventricles) and the subarachnoid space. The corpus callosum is a bundle of white matter fibers connecting the two cerebral hemispheres and does not contain CSF.

check_why_others_wrong.b: Lateral ventricles are the primary site of CSF production and circulation.
check_why_others_wrong.c: The fourth ventricle is part of the ventricular system where CSF flows before exiting to the subarachnoid space.
check_why_others_wrong.d: The subarachnoid space surrounds the brain and spinal cord and contains circulating CSF.

questions.question_text: The CSF is produced by choroid plexus present in: (2019).

options.label: c
options.text: Floor of posterior horn of lateral ventricle.

options.label: d
options.text: Lateral wall of inferior horn of lateral ventricle.

questions.check_explanation: The choroid plexus is located in the roof of the third ventricle (specifically the posterior part of the roof) and in the atria and horns of the lateral ventricles. It is not found on the floor of the third ventricle or the lateral walls of the inferior horn.

check_why_others_wrong.b: The floor of the third ventricle contains structures like the optic chiasm and mammillary bodies, not the choroid plexus.
check_why_others_wrong.c: The choroid plexus is located in the atrium (trigone) of the lateral ventricle, not the floor of the posterior horn.
check_why_others_wrong.d: The choroid plexus is located in the roof of the inferior horn, not the lateral wall.

questions.question_text: Arachnoid Villi: (2023).

options.label: a
options.text: Are situated in the spinal cord.

questions.check_explanation: Arachnoid villi (or granulations) are projections of the arachnoid mater into the dural venous sinuses that allow cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) to drain into the venous blood system.

check_why_others_wrong.a: They are primarily located in the cranial cavity, not the spinal cord.
check_why_others_wrong.b: CSF is produced by the choroid plexus, not the arachnoid villi.
check_why_others_wrong.d: They are projections of the arachnoid mater, not the dura mater.

questions.question_text: Concerning the cerebrospinal fluid, choose one correct answer: (DEP BOOK).

options.label: a
options.text: Produced mainly in the subarachnoid space.

options.label: c
options.text: Third ventricle has a choroid plexus in its roof.

options.label: d
options.text: Fourth ventricle has a choroid plexus in its floor.

questions.check_explanation: The choroid plexus is located in the roof of the third ventricle (specifically the tela choroidea) and is responsible for producing cerebrospinal fluid (CSF).

check_why_others_wrong.a: CSF is produced by the choroid plexus within the ventricles, not in the subarachnoid space.
check_why_others_wrong.b: Arachnoid granulations are responsible for the reabsorption of CSF into the venous sinuses, not its production.
check_why_others_wrong.d: The choroid plexus is located in the roof of the fourth ventricle, not the floor.

questions.question_text: Concerning the choroid plexus; choose one best answer: (DEP BOOK).

options.label: b
options.text: Is formed by a plexus of capillaries and a thin layer of cuboidal epithelium.

options.label: c
options.text: Is responsible for absorption of the cerebrospinal fluid.

options.label: d
options.text: All of the choroids plexuses are present in the floor of the ventricles.

questions.check_explanation: The choroid plexus is composed of a core of stroma containing a rich network of fenestrated capillaries covered by a single layer of cuboidal epithelial cells that produce cerebrospinal fluid (CSF).

check_why_others_wrong.a: The fourth ventricle does not contain a choroid plexus; it is formed by the fusion of the two lateral ventricles and the third ventricle.
check_why_others_wrong.c: The choroid plexus is responsible for the *production* (secretion) of CSF, not its absorption. Absorption occurs primarily via arachnoid villi/granulations.
check_why_others_wrong.d: Choroid plexuses are located in the lateral ventricles (attached to the septum pellucidum), the third ventricle (attached to the roof), and the fourth ventricle (though often described as absent or minimal in standard texts, the statement 'all... in the floor' is incorrect as they are generally on the roof or lateral walls).

questions.group_label: Arterial and venous supply of brain
questions.question_text: One of the following arteries is a branch of the basilar artery: (2019).
questions.check_explanation: The anterior inferior cerebellar artery (AICA) is a direct branch of the basilar artery. The posterior inferior cerebellar artery (PICA) arises from the vertebral artery, and the spinal arteries arise from the vertebral or basilar arteries but are not the primary named branches in this context compared to AICA.

check_why_others_wrong.b: The posterior inferior cerebellar artery (PICA) is a branch of the vertebral artery.
check_why_others_wrong.c: The anterior spinal artery is formed by branches from the vertebral arteries.
check_why_others_wrong.d: The posterior spinal arteries are branches of the vertebral arteries or PICA.

questions.group_label: Arterial and venous supply of brain
questions.question_text: One of the following arteries does not supply the internal capsule: (2018 - 2019).
questions.check_explanation: The internal capsule is supplied by lenticulostriate branches of the middle cerebral artery, the anterior choroidal artery, and the anterior cerebral artery (specifically the recurrent artery of Heubner). The posterior cerebral artery does not supply the internal capsule.

check_why_others_wrong.b: The anterior cerebral artery supplies the anterior limb of the internal capsule via the recurrent artery of Heubner.
check_why_others_wrong.c: The middle cerebral artery supplies the posterior limb and genu of the internal capsule via lenticulostriate branches.
check_why_others_wrong.d: The anterior choroidal artery supplies the posterior limb and retrolenticular part of the internal capsule.

questions.group_label: Arterial and venous supply of brain
questions.question_text: The main blood supply of the medial surface of the cerebrum is: (2018).
questions.check_explanation: The anterior cerebral artery (ACA) supplies the medial surface of the frontal and parietal lobes of the cerebrum.

check_why_others_wrong.a: The posterior inferior cerebellar artery supplies the cerebellum and medulla, not the cerebrum.
check_why_others_wrong.c: The middle cerebral artery supplies the lateral surface of the cerebral hemispheres.
check_why_others_wrong.d: The posterior cerebral artery supplies the occipital lobe and the inferior surface of the temporal lobe, not the main medial surface.

questions.group_label: Arterial and venous supply of brain
questions.question_text: Injury of which of the following arteries results in lateral medullary syndrome: (2017).
questions.check_explanation: Lateral medullary syndrome (Wallenberg syndrome) is caused by occlusion of the posterior inferior cerebellar artery (PICA) or the vertebral artery, leading to ischemia in the lateral medulla.

check_why_others_wrong.a: Superior cerebellar artery occlusion affects the superior cerebellum and midbrain/pons, not the lateral medulla.
check_why_others_wrong.c: Anterior inferior cerebellar artery occlusion affects the lateral pons (AICA syndrome).
check_why_others_wrong.d: Posterior cerebral artery occlusion affects the occipital lobe and thalamus.

questions.group_label: Arterial and venous supply of brain
questions.question_text: The choroid plexus of the 4th ventricle is derived from the following artery: (2017).
questions.check_explanation: The choroid plexus of the fourth ventricle is supplied by the posterior inferior cerebellar artery (PICA), specifically via its choroidal branches.

check_why_others_wrong.b: The anterior inferior cerebellar artery (AICA) supplies the lateral pons and anterior inferior cerebellum, not the 4th ventricle plexus.
check_why_others_wrong.c: The superior cerebellar artery (SCA) supplies the superior cerebellum and midbrain, not the 4th ventricle plexus.
check_why_others_wrong.d: The middle cerebral artery supplies the lateral surface of the cerebral hemispheres.

questions.group_label: Arterial and venous supply of brain
questions.question_text: A 65-year-old patient was admitted to the hospital in an unconscious condition. A CT scan examination revealed that the patient had suffered a cerebral vascular accident (stroke), with a small hematoma produced by the superior cerebellar artery. Which of the following nerves is most likely affected by the hematoma? (2017).
questions.check_explanation: The trochlear nerve (CN IV) has the longest intracranial course and passes over the superior cerebellar artery (SCA) as it exits the brainstem, making it highly susceptible to compression by an SCA hematoma or aneurysm.

check_why_others_wrong.b: The abducent nerve (CN VI) runs near the basilar artery and pons, not the SCA.
check_why_others_wrong.c: The facial nerve (CN VII) exits at the pontomedullary junction, far from the SCA.
check_why_others_wrong.d: The vestibulocochlear nerve (CN VIII) exits at the cerebellopontine angle, not near the SCA.

questions.group_label: Arterial and venous supply of brain
questions.question_text: The following artery shares in the supply of the medulla: (2016).
questions.check_explanation: The posterior inferior cerebellar artery (PICA) is a branch of the vertebral artery that supplies the lateral medulla oblongata. The other listed arteries supply the cerebellum, brainstem (pons/midbrain), or cerebral hemispheres, not the medulla.

check_why_others_wrong.b: The superior cerebellar artery supplies the superior surface of the cerebellum and the pons/midbrain, not the medulla.
check_why_others_wrong.c: The posterior cerebral artery supplies the occipital lobe, temporal lobe, and thalamus, not the medulla.
check_why_others_wrong.d: The middle cerebral artery supplies the lateral surface of the cerebral hemispheres, not the medulla.

questions.group_label: Arterial and venous supply of brain
questions.question_text: Branches of which cerebral artery vascularize the primary auditory cortex, Wernick’s area and angular gyrus: (DEP BOOK).
questions.check_explanation: The primary auditory cortex (Heschl's gyrus), Wernicke's area, and the angular gyrus are located in the temporal and parietal lobes, which are supplied by the middle cerebral artery (MCA).

check_why_others_wrong.a: Thalamogeniculate arteries supply the thalamus and internal capsule, not the cortical surface.
check_why_others_wrong.b: Anterior choroidal arteries supply the optic tract, posterior limb of the internal capsule, and parts of the temporal lobe, but not the primary auditory cortex or angular gyrus.
check_why_others_wrong.d: Anterior cerebral arteries supply the medial aspects of the frontal and parietal lobes.

questions.group_label: Arterial and venous supply of brain
questions.question_text: What is the major vessel lateral to optic chiasma: (DEP BOOK).
questions.check_explanation: The optic chiasma is located in the interpeduncular cistern. The anterior cerebral artery (A1 segment) runs along the medial aspect of the optic tract and is the major vessel immediately lateral to the optic chiasma. The posterior communicating artery is also nearby but is typically described as being posterior to the chiasma or lateral to the posterior aspect, while the A1 is the primary lateral landmark in standard anatomical descriptions for this region.

check_why_others_wrong.b: The posterior cerebral artery is located further posteriorly, near the midbrain and posterior perforating arteries.
check_why_others_wrong.c: The posterior communicating artery connects the internal carotid to the posterior cerebral artery and is situated posterior to the optic chiasma, not primarily lateral to the chiasm itself in the same direct manner as the A1.
check_why_others_wrong.d: The posterior inferior cerebellar artery is located in the posterior fossa, far from the optic chiasma.

questions.group_label: Arterial and venous supply of brain
questions.question_text: Anterior cerebral artery supplies: (DEP BOOK).
questions.check_explanation: The anterior cerebral artery (ACA) supplies the medial surface of the frontal and parietal lobes, which includes the paracentral lobule (motor and sensory areas for the lower limb).

check_why_others_wrong.b: The insula is primarily supplied by the middle cerebral artery (MCA).
check_why_others_wrong.c: The visual areas (occipital lobe) are supplied by the posterior cerebral artery (PCA).
check_why_others_wrong.d: Wernicke's area is located in the superior temporal gyrus and is supplied by the middle cerebral artery (MCA).

questions.group_label: Arterial and venous supply of brain
questions.question_text: Regarding the anterior cerebral artery, select the false statement: (2021 - IPKA).

options.label: a
options.text: Is a branch arises from the internal carotid artery.

options.label: b
options.text: Runs backwards along the upper surface of corpus callosum.

options.label: d
options.text: Supplies all parts of the corpus callosum, except the splenium.

questions.check_explanation: The anterior cerebral artery (ACA) does have central branches (perforating arteries) that supply the basal forebrain, including the head of the caudate nucleus and the anterior limb of the internal capsule. Therefore, the statement 'Has no central branches' is false.

check_why_others_wrong.a: The ACA is a direct branch of the internal carotid artery.
check_why_others_wrong.b: The ACA runs along the superior surface of the corpus callosum (in the interhemispheric fissure).
check_why_others_wrong.d: The ACA supplies the corpus callosum, but the splenium is typically supplied by the posterior cerebral artery (PCA).

questions.group_label: Arterial and venous supply of brain
questions.question_text: One of the following is a branch of the basilar artery: (2021 - 2023).
questions.check_explanation: The anterior inferior cerebellar artery (AICA) is a direct branch of the basilar artery. The posterior inferior cerebellar artery (PICA) arises from the vertebral artery.

check_why_others_wrong.b: PICA is a branch of the vertebral artery.
check_why_others_wrong.c: The anterior spinal artery is formed by branches from the vertebral arteries.
check_why_others_wrong.d: The posterior spinal arteries are branches of the vertebral or PICA.
check_why_others_wrong.e: The anterior cerebral artery is a branch of the internal carotid artery.
check_why_others_wrong.f: The middle cerebral artery is a branch of the internal carotid artery.

questions.group_label: Arterial and venous supply of brain
questions.question_text: One of the following arteries is not part of the circulus arteriosus: (2021 - IPKA).
questions.check_explanation: The Circle of Willis includes the anterior and posterior communicating arteries and the anterior cerebral arteries, but not the middle cerebral artery.

check_why_others_wrong.a: Anterior communicating artery is a component of the circle.
check_why_others_wrong.b: Posterior communicating artery is a component of the circle.
check_why_others_wrong.c: Anterior cerebral artery is a component of the circle.

questions.group_label: Arterial and venous supply of brain
questions.question_text: One of the following is a branch of the vertebral artery: (2020).
questions.check_explanation: The posterior inferior cerebellar artery (PICA) is the largest branch of the vertebral artery. The anterior cerebral and superior cerebellar arteries are branches of the internal carotid and basilar arteries, respectively, while the AICA is a branch of the basilar artery.

check_why_others_wrong.a: The anterior cerebral artery is a terminal branch of the internal carotid artery.
check_why_others_wrong.b: The anterior inferior cerebellar artery (AICA) is a branch of the basilar artery.
check_why_others_wrong.d: The superior cerebellar artery is a branch of the basilar artery.

questions.group_label: Arterial and venous supply of brain
questions.question_text: The middle cerebral artery supplies one of the following parts: (2020 – 2019 - 2024).

options.label: a
options.text: The retro-lentiform part of internal capsule.

options.label: b
options.text: Motor and sensory areas of the whole body.

options.label: c
options.text: Medial half of the orbital surface of the cerebral hemisphere.

options.label: e
options.text: The sublentiform part of internal capsule.

questions.check_explanation: The middle cerebral artery (MCA) supplies the lateral surface of the cerebral hemisphere, including the motor and sensory areas for the face and upper limb, and the sublentiform part of the internal capsule. The auditory area is supplied by the posterior cerebral artery (PCA).

check_why_others_wrong.a: The retrolentiform part of the internal capsule is supplied by the posterior cerebral artery (PCA).
check_why_others_wrong.b: The MCA supplies the face and upper limb areas, not the whole body (the lower limb is supplied by the anterior cerebral artery).
check_why_others_wrong.c: The medial half of the orbital surface is supplied by the anterior cerebral artery (ACA).
check_why_others_wrong.d: The auditory area (Heschl's gyrus) is located on the inferior temporal gyrus and is supplied by the posterior cerebral artery (PCA).

questions.group_label: Arterial and venous supply of brain
questions.question_text: Which one of the following vessels does not contribute to the circle of Willies: (2020).
questions.check_explanation: The circle of Willis is formed by the anterior communicating artery, the anterior cerebral arteries, the internal carotid arteries, the posterior communicating arteries, and the posterior cerebral arteries. The middle cerebral artery is a direct terminal branch of the internal carotid artery and does not participate in the formation of the circle.

check_why_others_wrong.b: The internal carotid artery is a primary component of the anterior part of the circle.
check_why_others_wrong.c: The anterior communicating artery connects the two anterior cerebral arteries and is a key component.
check_why_others_wrong.d: The posterior cerebral artery is a component of the posterior part of the circle.

questions.group_label: Arterial and venous supply of brain
questions.question_text: Which of the following arteries supply the Brocas area: (2023).
questions.check_explanation: Broca's area is located in the posterior part of the inferior frontal gyrus (Brodmann areas 44 and 45) on the lateral surface of the frontal lobe. This region is supplied by the superior and inferior divisions of the middle cerebral artery (MCA).

check_why_others_wrong.a: The anterior cerebral artery supplies the medial surface of the frontal lobe and the anterior part of the superior frontal gyrus, not the lateral inferior frontal gyrus.
check_why_others_wrong.c: The posterior cerebral artery supplies the occipital lobe and the inferior temporal lobe.
check_why_others_wrong.d: The vertebral artery supplies the brainstem and cerebellum, not the cerebral cortex directly.

questions.group_label: Arterial and venous supply of brain
questions.question_text: Concerning the cerebellum, select the true statement: (2023).

options.label: a
options.text: It lies in the middle cranial fossa.

options.label: b
options.text: Its upper surface is covered by falx cerebri.

options.label: c
options.text: Its superior vermis has a nodule and uvula only.

options.label: d
options.text: It's supplied by superior cerebellar artery.

questions.check_explanation: The cerebellum is located in the posterior cranial fossa, not the middle. Its superior surface is covered by the tentorium cerebelli, not the falx cerebri. The superior vermis includes the culmen, declive, folium, and tuber in addition to the nodule and uvula. The superior cerebellar artery is a major branch of the basilar artery that supplies the superior surface of the cerebellum.

check_why_others_wrong.a: The cerebellum is located in the posterior cranial fossa.
check_why_others_wrong.b: The falx cerebri separates the cerebral hemispheres; the tentorium cerebelli covers the superior surface of the cerebellum.
check_why_others_wrong.c: The superior vermis consists of multiple lobules (culmen, declive, folium, tuber, nodule, uvula), not just the nodule and uvula.

questions.group_label: Arterial and venous supply of brain
questions.question_text: Concerning the superficial middle cerebral vein choose one best answer: (2024).

options.label: a
options.text: It lies in the posterior ramus of the lateral sulcus.

options.label: b
options.text: It receives the majority of inferior cerebral veins of the medial surface.

options.label: d
options.text: Ends in the superior sagittal sinus.

questions.check_explanation: The superficial middle cerebral vein (Sylvian vein) runs in the anterior ramus of the lateral sulcus (Sylvian fissure) and drains into the cavernous sinus. Option A is the only anatomically plausible statement among the choices, as the vein is located in the lateral sulcus (though technically the anterior ramus, 'posterior' is likely a typo or distractor, but B, C, and D are factually incorrect regarding drainage or location).

check_why_others_wrong.b: It drains the lateral surface of the hemisphere, not the medial surface.
check_why_others_wrong.c: It typically drains into the cavernous sinus, not the transverse sinus.
check_why_others_wrong.d: It does not drain into the superior sagittal sinus.

questions.group_label: Arterial and venous supply of brain
questions.question_text: Regarding the arterial supply of the brain, one of the following is true: (DEP BOOK).

options.label: a
options.text: The areas of smell and vision are supplied by the middle cerebral artery.

options.label: b
options.text: The cerebellum is supplied by branches of the internal carotid system.

options.label: c
options.text: The anterior inferior cerebellar artery shares in the arterial supply of the medulla.

options.label: d
options.text: The auditory and speech areas are supplied by branches of the middle cerebral artery.

questions.check_explanation: The primary auditory cortex (Heschl's gyrus) and Broca's area (speech production) are located in the temporal and frontal lobes, respectively, both of which are supplied by the middle cerebral artery (MCA).

check_why_others_wrong.a: The olfactory areas are supplied by the anterior cerebral artery (ACA), and the visual cortex is supplied by the posterior cerebral artery (PCA).
check_why_others_wrong.b: The cerebellum is supplied by branches of the vertebrobasilar system (posterior circulation), not the internal carotid system (anterior circulation).
check_why_others_wrong.c: The anterior inferior cerebellar artery (AICA) supplies the lateral pons and cerebellum, not the medulla (which is supplied by the posterior inferior cerebellar artery and vertebral branches).

questions.group_label: Arterial and venous supply of brain
questions.question_text: Concerning the superficial middle cerebral vein choose one best answer:  (DEP BOOK).

options.label: a
options.text: It lies in the posterior ramus of the lateral sulcus.

options.label: b
options.text: It receives the majority of inferior cerebral veins of the medial surface.

options.label: d
options.text: Ends in the superior sagittal sinus.

questions.check_explanation: The superficial middle cerebral vein (Sylvian vein) runs in the anterior part of the lateral sulcus (Sylvian fissure), which is the anterior ramus. It drains the superficial parts of the frontal, parietal, and temporal lobes and typically empties into the cavernous sinus or the sphenoparietal sinus.

check_why_others_wrong.b: It drains the lateral surface of the brain, not the medial surface (which is drained by veins like the basal vein of Rosenthal or internal cerebral veins).
check_why_others_wrong.c: It does not end in the transverse sinus; it usually ends in the cavernous sinus or sphenoparietal sinus.
check_why_others_wrong.d: It does not end in the superior sagittal sinus; that is the destination for superior cerebral veins.

questions.group_label: Arterial and venous supply of brain
questions.question_text: The anterior cerebral artery supplies: (DEP BOOK).

options.label: a
options.text: The motor and sensory areas of the upper and lower limbs.

options.label: b
options.text: The occipital lobe of the brain.

options.label: c
options.text: All parts of the internal capsule.

options.label: d
options.text: All parts of the corpus callosum, except splenium.

questions.check_explanation: The anterior cerebral artery (ACA) supplies the medial surface of the frontal and parietal lobes, which includes the motor and sensory areas for the lower limb. It also supplies the anterior two-thirds of the corpus callosum (genu and body), while the splenium is supplied by the posterior cerebral artery (PCA).

check_why_others_wrong.a: The ACA supplies the lower limb areas, but the upper limb areas are supplied by the middle cerebral artery (MCA).
check_why_others_wrong.b: The occipital lobe is supplied by the posterior cerebral artery (PCA).
check_why_others_wrong.c: The internal capsule is supplied by lenticulostriate branches of the MCA (anterior and posterior limbs) and the anterior choroidal artery (retrolenticular part), not the ACA.

questions.group_label: Arterial and venous supply of brain
questions.question_text: The posterior cerebral artery supplies one of the following structures: (DEP BOOK).

options.label: c
options.text: Lateral half of orbital surface of cerebral hemisphere.

options.label: d
options.text: Main part of the lateral surface of the hemisphere.

questions.check_explanation: The posterior cerebral artery (PCA) supplies the splenium of the corpus callosum, the medial and inferior surfaces of the occipital and temporal lobes, and the thalamus. The insula and lateral surfaces are supplied by the middle cerebral artery (MCA).

check_why_others_wrong.b: The insula is supplied by the middle cerebral artery (MCA).
check_why_others_wrong.c: The lateral half of the orbital surface is supplied by the anterior cerebral artery (ACA) or MCA, not the PCA.
check_why_others_wrong.d: The main part of the lateral surface of the hemisphere is supplied by the middle cerebral artery (MCA).

questions.group_label: Arterial and venous supply of brain
questions.question_text: The middle cerebral artery supplies one of the following parts: (DEP BOOK).

options.label: b
options.text: The sublentiform part of internal capsule.

options.label: c
options.text: Motor and sensory areas of the whole body.

options.label: d
options.text: Medial half of orbital surface of cerebral hemisphere.

questions.check_explanation: The middle cerebral artery (MCA) supplies the lateral surface of the cerebral hemisphere, which contains the motor and sensory areas for the face and upper limb (contralateral). While it does not supply the *whole* body (the medial leg area is supplied by the ACA), option C is the standard correct answer in this context compared to the other specific errors. Option A is supplied by the posterior cerebral artery (PCA). Option B is supplied by the anterior choroidal artery. Option D is supplied by the anterior cerebral artery (ACA).

check_why_others_wrong.a: The auditory area (Heschl's gyrus) is located in the temporal lobe and is supplied by the posterior cerebral artery (PCA).
check_why_others_wrong.b: The sublentiform part of the internal capsule is supplied by the anterior choroidal artery.
check_why_others_wrong.d: The medial half of the orbital surface is supplied by the anterior cerebral artery (ACA).

questions.group_label: Arterial and venous supply of brain
questions.question_text: Branches of which cerebral artery vascularize the primary auditory cortex, Wernick’s area and angular gyrus: (DEP BOOK).
questions.check_explanation: The primary auditory cortex, Wernicke's area, and the angular gyrus are located in the superior temporal gyrus and inferior parietal lobule, which are supplied by the superior and inferior divisions of the middle cerebral artery (MCA).

check_why_others_wrong.a: Thalamogeniculate arteries supply the thalamus, not the cortical surface.
check_why_others_wrong.b: The anterior cerebral artery supplies the medial frontal and parietal lobes.
check_why_others_wrong.d: The anterior choroidal artery supplies the internal capsule, optic tract, and parts of the temporal lobe, but not the primary auditory cortex or Wernicke's area.

questions.question_text: The neural tube gives rise to which of the following cells: (2018).
questions.check_explanation: The neural tube differentiates into the central nervous system, including the ventral horn motor neurons (lower motor neurons). The other options are derived from neural crest cells.

check_why_others_wrong.a: Sympathetic trunk cells are derived from neural crest cells.
check_why_others_wrong.b: Suprarenal medulla cells (chromaffin cells) are derived from neural crest cells.
check_why_others_wrong.c: Dorsal root ganglion cells are sensory neurons derived from neural crest cells.

questions.question_text: Infundibulum is a downward extension of the: (2016).
questions.check_explanation: The infundibulum (pituitary stalk) is a downward projection from the hypothalamus, which is part of the diencephalon, connecting it to the neurohypophysis.

check_why_others_wrong.a: The prosencephalon is the forebrain vesicle that gives rise to both the telencephalon and diencephalon, but the infundibulum specifically arises from the diencephalon.
check_why_others_wrong.b: The telencephalon gives rise to the cerebral hemispheres, not the infundibulum.
check_why_others_wrong.c: The rhombencephalon gives rise to the hindbrain structures (medulla, pons, cerebellum), not the infundibulum.

questions.question_text: Of the following, the one most closely associated with the cerebrum is:(DEP BOOK).
questions.check_explanation: The cerebrum develops from the telencephalon, the most anterior vesicle of the embryonic neural tube.

check_why_others_wrong.b: The diencephalon gives rise to the thalamus, hypothalamus, and epithalamus, not the cerebrum.
check_why_others_wrong.c: The mesencephalon gives rise to the midbrain.
check_why_others_wrong.d: The metencephalon gives rise to the pons and cerebellum.

questions.question_text: Of the following, the one most closely associated with the 3rd ventricle is:  (DEP BOOK).
questions.check_explanation: The third ventricle is a cavity located within the diencephalon, specifically between the two thalami.

check_why_others_wrong.a: The telencephalon contains the lateral ventricles.
check_why_others_wrong.c: The mesencephalon contains the cerebral aqueduct.
check_why_others_wrong.d: The metencephalon contains the fourth ventricle.

questions.question_text: Which spinal cord layer contains cell bodies and astrocytes? (DEP BOOK).
questions.check_explanation: The spinal cord is histologically divided into the marginal layer (white matter, axons) and the mantle layer (gray matter, cell bodies). The mantle layer contains the neuronal cell bodies and associated glial cells, including astrocytes.

check_why_others_wrong.a: The ventricular layer is not a standard histological layer of the spinal cord; it refers to the lining of the central canal.
check_why_others_wrong.b: The ependyma is the epithelial lining of the central canal, not a layer containing neuronal cell bodies.
check_why_others_wrong.d: The marginal layer consists primarily of white matter (myelinated axons) and lacks neuronal cell bodies.

questions.question_text: The brain flexure which develops between the metencephalon and the myelencephalon is called the: (DEP BOOK).
questions.check_explanation: The pontine flexure is the specific brain flexure that develops between the metencephalon (pons and cerebellum) and the myelencephalon (medulla oblongata).

check_why_others_wrong.a: Midbrain is a primary brain vesicle, not a flexure.
check_why_others_wrong.b: Hindbrain is the general region containing the metencephalon and myelencephalon, not the flexure itself.
check_why_others_wrong.c: The cervical flexure is located between the myelencephalon and the spinal cord.
check_why_others_wrong.d: The cephalic (optic) flexure is located between the telencephalon and diencephalon.

questions.question_text: Regarding the development of the spinal cord, the following are correct statement except: (2020).

options.label: a
options.text: White matter of the spinal cord develops in the marginal zone.

options.label: b
options.text: Dorsal root ganglia are derived from the neural crest cells.

options.label: c
options.text: At birth spinal cord ends at the level of the first lumbar vertebra.

options.label: d
options.text: Mantle zone gives rise to the grey matter of the spinal cord.

questions.check_explanation: At birth, the conus medullaris (end of the spinal cord) typically terminates at the level of the L3 vertebra, not L1. The L1 level is characteristic of the adult spinal cord.

check_why_others_wrong.a: The marginal zone is the outer layer of the neural tube that differentiates into white matter.
check_why_others_wrong.b: Dorsal root ganglia are derived from neural crest cells that migrate from the neural tube.
check_why_others_wrong.d: The mantle zone is the inner layer of the neural tube that differentiates into grey matter.

questions.question_text: Regarding the development of the central nervous system, mark one correct statement: (DEP BOOK)

options.label: a
options.text: It appears as a thickened ectodermal neural plate

options.label: b
options.text: Prosencephalon gives rise to metencephalon and diencephalon

options.label: c
options.text: Cervical ﬂexure appears at the junction of hindbrain and spinal cord

options.label: d
options.text: Myelencephalon will form pons and cerebellum

questions.question_text: Regarding the development of the central nervous system, mark one correct statement: (DEP BOOK)

options.label: a
options.text: The cephalic part of the neural tube remains narrow

options.label: b
options.text: Its neuropores establish a temporary connection of the neural tube with the amnion

options.label: c
options.text: The telencephalon forms pons and cerebellum

questions.check_explanation: None of the provided options are correct. The cephalic neural tube widens (ventricles), neuropores close to seal the tube (not connect to amnion), the telencephalon forms the cerebrum (not pons/cerebellum), and the myelencephalon forms the medulla (not midbrain).

check_why_others_wrong.a: The cephalic part of the neural tube dilates to form the ventricles of the brain.
check_why_others_wrong.b: Neuropores close to seal the neural tube; they do not establish a connection with the amnion.
check_why_others_wrong.c: The telencephalon forms the cerebrum (cerebral hemispheres); the pons and cerebellum derive from the metencephalon.
check_why_others_wrong.d: The myelencephalon forms the medulla oblongata; the midbrain derives from the mesencephalon.

questions.question_text: Regarding the development of the brain, mark one correct statement: (DEP BOOK)

options.label: a
options.text: The telencephalon gives rise to thalamus and hypothalamus

options.label: b
options.text: Metencephalon gives rise to medulla oblongata

options.label: c
options.text: The cavity of the rhombencephalon is known as fourth ventricle

options.label: d
options.text: The cavity of the mesencephalon is known as lateral ventricle

questions.check_explanation: The rhombencephalon (hindbrain) develops into the metencephalon and myelencephalon, and its central canal dilates to form the fourth ventricle. The telencephalon forms the cerebral hemispheres (not thalamus/hypothalamus), the metencephalon forms the pons and cerebellum (not medulla), and the mesencephalon's cavity is the cerebral aqueduct (not lateral ventricle).

check_why_others_wrong.a: Thalamus and hypothalamus arise from the diencephalon, not the telencephalon.
check_why_others_wrong.b: The medulla oblongata arises from the myelencephalon, not the metencephalon.
check_why_others_wrong.d: The cavity of the mesencephalon is the cerebral aqueduct; the lateral ventricles are in the telencephalon.

questions.question_text: Regarding the development of the spinal cord, mark one correct answer: (DEP BOOK)

options.label: a
options.text: Grey matter of the spinal cord  develops in the marginal zone

options.label: b
options.text: Dorsal root ganglia are derived from the neural crest cells

options.label: c
options.text: At birth spinal cord ends at the level of the ﬁrst lumbar vertebra

options.label: d
options.text: Mantle zone gives rise to the white matter of the spinal cord

questions.check_explanation: Dorsal root ganglia are derived from neural crest cells, which migrate from the neural tube during embryonic development. The other options contain factual errors regarding spinal cord anatomy and development.

check_why_others_wrong.a: Grey matter develops from the mantle zone (neuroepithelium), not the marginal zone (which becomes white matter).
check_why_others_wrong.c: At birth, the spinal cord ends at the level of the third lumbar vertebra (L3), not the first (L1).
check_why_others_wrong.d: The mantle zone gives rise to the grey matter, while the marginal zone gives rise to the white matter.

questions.question_text: Regarding the development of the spinal cord, mark one correct answer: (DEP BOOK)

options.label: a
options.text: Dorsal root ganglia are derived from the neural tube

options.label: b
options.text: At birth spinal cord ends at the level of the second lumbar vertebra

options.label: c
options.text: Spina biﬁda occulta is a condition in which there is failure of the lamina to fuse in three successive vertebrae

options.label: d
options.text: Meningocele is the condition in which spina biﬁda is associated with herniation of meninges

questions.check_explanation: Meningocele is a type of spina bifida where the meninges herniate through a vertebral defect, forming a sac. The other options contain factual errors regarding embryology, anatomy, or definitions.

check_why_others_wrong.a: Dorsal root ganglia are derived from the neural crest, not the neural tube.
check_why_others_wrong.b: At birth, the spinal cord typically ends at the level of the third lumbar vertebra (L3), not L2.
check_why_others_wrong.c: Spina bifida occulta is typically a failure of the lamina to fuse in a single vertebra, not three successive ones.

questions.question_text: Regarding the development of the spinal cord, mark one correct answer: (DEP BOOK).

options.label: a
options.text: Basal plate forms the sensory areas of the spinal cord

options.label: b
options.text: Alar plate forms the motor areas of the spinal cord

options.label: c
options.text: Sulcus limitans marks the boundary between motor and sensory areas

options.label: d
options.text: The roof and ﬂoor plates are thick

questions.check_explanation: The sulcus limitans is the embryological groove that separates the alar plate (sensory) from the basal plate (motor) in the neural tube. The basal plate forms motor areas, the alar plate forms sensory areas, and the roof and floor plates are thin epithelial structures.

check_why_others_wrong.a: The basal plate forms motor (efferent) areas, not sensory.
check_why_others_wrong.b: The alar plate forms sensory (afferent) areas, not motor.
check_why_others_wrong.d: The roof and floor plates are thin, not thick.
